components.assessment: Exponent reduction and inverse closure identify the monomial span with the actual coordinate field. Spanning plus degree p^2 constructs the basis. Basis-product weights prove the product rule; diagonality proves commutation and eigenspace classification.

The actual witness yields two Euler equations. Nonmonomiality proves nonzero derivatives and nonconstant nonzero corrections A,B. Differentiation and elimination force DA/A=EB/B. One-variable memberships force a scalar eigenvalue; injective residue casts force the same nonzero m for both coordinates.

For n=p-m, S=X^n+c_X X^p=X^n U/DU is nonzero. Equality of logarithmic derivatives puts U^n/S in the nonzero scalar kernel. Coefficients t_X*c_X*X^p and t_X are both nonzero. The Y calculation uses the same n; p=2 is included.

An unqualified affine identity at r forces correction weight -r, even though its coefficient hypothesis allows zero. Nonzero correction and weight m give m+r=0 in characteristic p, hence r=p-m. Either input separately determines the exponent.

components.assessment: For W=sum k X^iY^j, exponent reduction gives multiplication closure and Frobenius gives w^p=sum c_ij^p (X^p)^i (Y^p)^j in k. Nonzero w has inverse w^(p-1)/w^p in W, so W=k(X,Y). The degree condition gives a basis and every witness object lies there. No condition on ambient p-th powers outside this field is needed.

The actual Frobenius coefficient field, degree notion of p-independence, scalar-monomial exclusion, genuine witness, shared exponent, coefficient nonvanishing and uniqueness from either inclusion match the pinned original proposition.
